L131.d: The celestial musicians produce celestial harmony by manipulating seven spirit forces: spiritual sound, spiritual light, energy impingements, color symphonies, the harmony of associated spirits, the melody of thought, and the music of space. It is striking that not only sound but light, color, the arrangement of beings, and even thought become music. Color symphonies rank among the highest accomplishments of the celestial musicians, and spiritual thinking can be so perfected as to burst forth in the melodies of Havona. Harmony, the music of the seven levels of melodious association, is the one universal code of spirit communication. Music as Urantia mortals understand it attains its highest expression in the schools of Jerusem, but mortals do not react to the other forms of morontia melody. The author says that the best music of Urantia is just a fleeting echo of the magnificent strains of heaven.

L132.d: The heavenly reproducers, the second division of the celestial artisans, preserve and reproduce the past and the present. The singers reiterate the harmonies of the past; the color workers preserve passing scenes like sketchers and painters; the light picturizers make preservations of which motion pictures are a very crude illustration. The historic pageanteers dramatize the crucial events of universe history, and the prophetic artists project the meanings of history into the future. The life-story tellers project present personal experience into future attainment values, and the administrative enactors portray the philosophy of government. They collaborate with the reversion directors in combining memory recapitulation with mind rest, and the author once witnessed a production in which over one million actors presented a thousand successive scenes. Memory, history, and story are vital materials of ascendant education.

L133.d: There are cities whose builder and maker is God. The author says that in spirit counterpart the morontia and spirit worlds have all that mortals are familiar with and inexpressibly more. The divine builders construct their homes, workplaces, places of play, temples, schools, and halls of common assembly. These morontia and spirit domiciles are real, and to a certain extent every spirit being may participate with the builders in planning and constructing his own abode. The transition worlds have an essential economy of mutual ministry and specialized labor, and enormous edifices for rest and recreation, including settings for the reversion directors. All worlds of mortal ascent have temples of worship, the most exquisite creations of the morontia realms. Though invisible to physical eyes, life there is a whole life of home, work, play, worship, and learning.

L134.d: The thought recorders are artisans devoted to preserving and reproducing the superior thought of the realms. The thought preservers treasure the gems of mentation in the tongue of Uversa. Concept recorders preserve idea patterns, by which one may gain in an hour more than a century of ordinary reading would yield. Ideograph recorders, promoters of oratory, broadcast directors, the rhythm recorders whom we would call poets, and the morontia recorders, the group photographers of the transition worlds, complete the list. Expert recorders can register over five hundred thousand thought symbols a minute, and in the language of Nebadon a half-hour address can cover the subject matter of a mortal lifetime. The comfort of this list is that our best thoughts are not lost but preserved as a universe heritage.

L135.d: The energy manipulators are celestial artisans concerned with every kind of energy: physical, mindal, and spiritual. The first three each specialize in one kind. Physical-energy manipulators serve with the power directors, and mind-energy manipulators promote communication between different types of intelligent beings. The account of the spiritual-energy manipulators is notable: spiritual energy, like physical energy, acts in accordance with established laws and can be studied and manipulated with reliable results. The compound manipulators seek to associate all three energies and are in reality seeking the universe presence of God the Supreme, in whom such unification must occur. Then come the transport advisers, the experts of communication, and the teachers of rest; seventy transport advisers and twelve communication technicians serve on Urantia. The final item, that divine rest is a technique of spiritual-energy intake, reminds us that even rest is part of spiritual growth.

L136.d: The designers and embellishers embrace over one thousand subdivisions of activity grouped under seven major heads: craftworkers of color, sound designers, emotion designers, artists of odor, presence embellishers, taste designers, and morontia synthesizers. The author repeatedly laments that he does not know how to portray the exquisite work of these unique artisans; even the name artists of odor is an unfortunate comparison, used because mortals could hardly recognize this ministry by any other. The presence embellishers dramatize the significance of relationship through the arrangement of diverse beings, arranging them like living musical notes and blending them into anthems of glory. Finally the morontia synthesizers add the culminating touches to every ensemble. Color, sound, emotion, odor, and taste all serve beauty, and to begin to imagine that glory, the author concludes, we must await deliverance from the animal body.

L137.d: The seven major worlds swinging around Jerusem are known as the transitional culture spheres. Each is surrounded by seven satellites, and those surrounding the first, the Finaliter World, are the seven mansion worlds. As ascenders advance from one mansion world to the next, they become eligible to visit the corresponding transition world, so that morontia life becomes ever-widening contact with universe society. Visits to the Finaliter World are designed to foster faith in the ultimate destiny of transition mortals. The list proceeds through the Finaliter, Morontia, Angelic, Superangel, Sons, and Spirit worlds to the World of the Father. This is the silent sphere where no group of beings is domiciled; in its great temple of light no one can be discerned, yet all beings are welcome as worshipers. In Satania its satellites now serve as detention spheres for the Lucifer rebels.

L138.d: The System Sovereign, chief executive of a local system, is normally supported by two or three Lanonandek Sons serving as first and second assistants. Satania, however, is now administered by a staff of seven Lanonandeks, an expanded emergency administration made necessary by the exigencies of the Lucifer rebellion. Lanaforge, the System Sovereign, is successor to the apostate Lucifer, and the two assistant Sovereigns, the custodian, and the recorder came to Satania with him. Holdant, the custodian, holds all interned spirits above the order of mortal existence, while Fortant, the bestowal director, oversees the universe activities transplanted to Jerusem since Michael's bestowal on Urantia. Hanavard, the high counselor, is the twelfth of his order to serve thus since the rebellion. Through concrete names and numbers the list shows how rebellion reshaped even the form of system government.

L139.d: Since the system is a unit of administration rather than adjudication, there are only minor courts on Jerusem. Instead, the Lanonandek administration is supported by the Jerusem executive council, the supreme advisory body of Satania. The first three of its twelve members are Hanavard, the Lanonandek chairman, Lanaforge, the System Sovereign, and Mansurotia, the first assistant Sovereign. The other nine represent the Melchizedeks, Life Carriers, finaliters, Material Sons, seraphim, physical controllers, Morontia Power Supervisors, midway creatures, and ascending mortals. Nearly every major order involved in system affairs sits at one table. Notice that the original Adam of Satania sits as supervising head of the Material Sons, and the acting head of the ascending mortals takes the last seat. The council chooses representatives to the supreme council at universe headquarters, but this representation is now suspended by rebellion.

L140.d: At the center of the seven angelic residential circles on Jerusem is the Urantia advisory council, the four and twenty elders whom John the Revelator saw about the throne. These counselors were recruited from the eight Urantia races, and the last of them were assembled at the resurrection roll call of Michael. The first eight led their races to higher concepts of Deity: The Breath Giver, The Great Spirit, One Truth, The God of Gods, and others. Then come Adam and Eve, Enoch, Moses, Elijah, Machiventa Melchizedek, John the Baptist, and 1-2-3 the First, leader of the loyal midwayers, completing the sixteen permanent members. The remaining eight seats are temporarily filled while held open for ascenders of the postbestowal age and the great teachers of future ages. The list shows how humanity's spiritual progress has been carried by named individuals of many races and ages.

L141.d: Considerable portions of Jerusem are residential, while other portions serve the administration of 619 inhabited spheres, 56 transition culture worlds, and the system capital itself. This list shows the arrangement in four geometric forms. The circles are the residential areas of nonnative beings; the squares serve system executive and administrative functions; the rectangles are the rendezvous of the lower native life; and the triangles serve the local administration of Jerusem itself. This arrangement is common to all the system capitals of Nebadon, though in another universe an entirely different plan might prevail, according to the designs of the Creator Sons. The system capitals are the only worlds exhibiting well-nigh perfectly all three phases of universe existence, material, morontial, and spiritual, so that material, morontia, and spirit personalities alike feel at home on Jerusem. The list pictures a heavenly city designed for both order and beauty.

L142.d: The Jerusem circles are the residential reservations assigned to the major groups of universe life at the system capital. The narrative names seven: the Sons of God, the angels and higher spirits, the Universe Aids, the Master Physical Controllers, the assigned ascending mortals, the courtesy colonies, and the Corps of the Finality. Each residential grouping consists of seven concentric and successively elevated circles, built along the same lines but of different sizes and materials. Notably, ascending mortals and midway creatures have their own place beside divine Sons and spirits. Jerusem is a miniature of universe society, where many orders of beings keep their own abodes while living together in one capital.

L143.d: The executive-administrative divisions of the system are located in one thousand immense departmental squares on Jerusem, clustered into ten grand divisions that form the ten departments listed here. The order begins with the maintenance of physical power and energy, passes through arbitration and ethics, planetary, constellation, and universe affairs, education and science, and ends with morontia affairs, pure spirit activities, ascendant ministry, and grand universe philosophy. The arrangement widens from matter to spirit and from local concerns to the grand universe. These structures are transparent, so that all system activities can be viewed even by student visitors. System administration is not hidden power but an open service from which anyone may learn.

L144.d: The creation of the first Morontia Power Supervisors coincides with the arrival of the first mortal survivor on a first mansion world of a local universe. They are created in groups of one thousand, divided into seven classes. Circuit Regulators are the largest, four hundred; System Co-ordinators number two hundred; Planetary Custodians, Combined Controllers, and Liaison Stabilizers one hundred each; Selective Assorters and Associate Registrars fifty each. The proportions show that regulating the morontia energy circuits is their chief work. Power supervisors always serve in their native universe and are directed exclusively by the joint spirit activity of the Universe Son and the Universe Spirit. The list reveals an unseen foundation the universe provides in advance for mortal ascent.

L145.d: The Morontia Companions are the local universe beings who live closest to ascending mortals on the mansion worlds. The narrative classifies their activities in a local system under seven heads, giving an idea of the nature of their work. It begins with the Pilgrim Guardians who co-ordinate the whole career and continues with the receivers who welcome you on awakening, the hosts to visitors, the directors of social conduct and classes, the language teachers and interpreters, the excursion supervisors, and the custodians of buildings. Striking is the remark that you will learn a language over there much as you do down here. Companions are not assigned permanently but according to need and supply. The morontia career is a social life of learning in warm fellowship.

L146.t: Three General Levels of Spirit Humor

Prophetic joy

L146.d: In discussing the reversion directors of the mansion worlds, an angelic author explains spirit humor, first by telling what it is not: spirit jest never accentuates the misfortunes of the weak and erring, nor is it blasphemous of divine righteousness. Then come three levels. Reminiscent jests draw on memories of the past to lighten present loads; current humor discovers the senselessness of much present anxiety; prophetic joy arises from assurance about the future. The sequence of past, present, and future is clear. The highest level grows out of faith in the loving overcare of superiors and in the divine stability of the Supreme Directors. True humor is a rest of mind born of faith, and it helps recuperate depleted energies.

L147.d: The transition seraphim are angels who labor untiringly on the mansion worlds for the advancement of their mortal pupils, though you will not be conscious of their ministry until you attain those worlds. They serve in seven divisions: evangels who help choose ascension routes, racial interpreters, mind planners who organize morontia teamwork, morontia counselors, technicians who aid adjustment to new surroundings, recorder-teachers of the borderland transactions, and the ministering reserves. The evangels proclaim the great law of the conservation and dominance of goodness: no act of good is ever wholly lost. The spirit world respects freewill choice provided the course is not detrimental to you or injurious to your fellows. Mansion world education is a careful ministry that honors individual differences and choices.

L148.d: Mota is the philosophy of the morontia level, and beginners on the mansion worlds approach it by way of familiar human philosophy. An angelic author records twenty-eight statements of human philosophy that a morontia instructor on the first mansion world used as illustrative material. Pairs such as cleverness and character, faith and fear, effort and happiness, affliction and wisdom, ambition and virtue, knowledge and sharing are set together in brief sayings. Though the topics seem scattered, one thread runs through them: inner motive and experience, more than outward skill, shape the soul. The evolving soul is not made divine by what it does, but by what it strives to do. Earthly wisdom becomes a ladder toward morontia insight.

L149.d: Each system has a standard and basic pattern of vegetable and animal life, but the Life Carriers must often modify it to conform to the varying physical conditions of the worlds of space. The result is seven distinct physical types with thousands upon thousands of minor variants. The greatest differences arise from the atmosphere; the Urantia races are average mid-breathers and belong to the land order. Gravity, temperature, electric, and energizing differences follow, and the rest are grouped as unnamed types. The narrative stresses that all these differences are matters of anatomy and physiology and have nothing to do with intellectual or spiritual life. However varied in form, all mortals alike enjoy the ministry of Thought Adjusters and guardian angels. Beneath physical diversity lies spiritual equality.

L150.t: Seven Viewpoints for Studying Planetary Mortals

Brain-type series

Planetary-mortal epochs
Creature-kinship serials
Adjuster-fusion series

L150.d: Because we know so little about the planetary series of mortals and because there are so many variations, an adequate portrayal of them is difficult. The narrative therefore first sets out seven viewpoints from which mortal creatures may be studied, and the following discussion is arranged accordingly: adjustment to planetary environment, brain type, spirit reception, planetary epochs, creature kinship, Adjuster fusion, and the techniques of terrestrial escape. The first two concern differences of body and mind, the next four spiritual progress and historical stages, and the last the path beyond death. This is a method of cosmic anthropology that understands man not by a single measure but from many angles.

L151.d: All mortals alike are liberated from the bonds of flesh and go to the morontia worlds, yet there are five orders of terrestrial escape. In the early ages most are sleeping survivors repersonalized at the dispensational roll calls. Those who attain the third circle receive personal guardians of destiny and awaken on the first mansion world on the third day. Children who die young follow the more advanced parent to the probationary nursery. Mortals of more advanced worlds pass by the mansion worlds but must later journey back as instructors, and the most advanced fuse with their Adjusters during life and are translated without death. As a planet advances toward light and life, natural death becomes decreasingly frequent. The path beyond death opens according to the spiritual maturity of the world and of the individual.

L152.t: Five Pursuits at the Prince's Headquarters Settlement
rows: Physical labor
Cultivation of the soil, associated with home building and embellishment
Social activities

Educational application

Vocational training
Schools of marriage and homemaking, art and craft, and the training of teachers
Spiritual culture
The teacher brotherhood, enlightenment of youth, training native children as missionaries
L152.d: In the headquarters settlement of a Planetary Prince every habitation was provided with abundance of land, and the students and teachers in the Prince's schools were all agriculturists and horticulturists. Their time was about equally divided among five pursuits: physical labor in soil cultivation and home building, social activities of plays and cultural gatherings, educational application in family and class teaching, vocational training in marriage, crafts, and teacher preparation, and spiritual culture through the teacher brotherhood and missionary training. Body, society, intellect, skill, and spirit receive balanced attention. Native children trained in these schools returned to their peoples and founded new centers of learning and culture, so that a civilizing influence gradually radiated to all. A balanced daily life is the foundation of civilizing education.

L153.t: Seven Developmental Epochs of the Mortal Races

Chiefly concerned with food problems
The security age

The era of light and life
Human accomplishments blended in cosmic unity and unselfish service
L153.d: Under the benign rule of a Planetary Prince, augmented by the Material Sons and punctuated by the missions of the Paradise Sons, the mortal races of an average world pass successively through seven developmental epochs. From the nutrition epoch of seeking food, the security age, and the material-comfort era, they advance to the quest for knowledge and wisdom, the epoch of philosophy and brotherhood, the age of spiritual striving, and finally the era of light and life. The order follows a hierarchy of needs: intellect, ethics, and spirit grow only after survival and security are assured. The last epoch is the flowering in which earlier achievements are blended in cosmic unity and unselfish service. The progress of civilization is not chance but growth unfolding by stages according to a divine plan.

The Creator Son and supreme ruler of the local creations
The super-Fathers
The Ancients of Days who govern the superuniverse
The spirit or Havona Father
The Universal Father, who dwells on Paradise
L154.d: As the progeny of the Material Son and Daughter blend with the races of men, they become accepted as the common ancestors of mankind. In this context the narrative says that mortals who start out from an inhabited world are intended to have the experience of recognizing seven fathers. The series begins with the father in the flesh and passes through the Planetary Adam, the System Sovereign, the Constellation Father, the Creator Son, and the Ancients of Days, reaching the Universal Father. The order matches the stages of universe administration through which ascending mortals pass: home, planet, system, constellation, local universe, superuniverse, and Paradise. The last Father bestows his spirit to live in the minds of lowly creatures. Fatherhood is a principle of relationship running through the whole universe.

rows: Pre-Planetary Prince Man
Post-Planetary Prince Man
Post-Adamic Man
Post-Magisterial Son Man
Post-Bestowal Son Man
Post-Teacher Son Man
The Era of Light and Life
L155.d: From the inception of life on an evolutionary planet to its final flowering in the era of light and life, at least seven epochs of human life appear upon the stage of world action. These ages are determined by the planetary missions of the divine Sons. The arrival of the Planetary Prince, the coming of the Material Son and Daughter, the mission of a Magisterial Son, the bestowal of a Paradise Son, and the visitation of the Trinity Teacher Sons successively mark the boundaries of the epochs. The period from life initiation to the appearance of man is set apart as the prehuman era and precedes the list. Since Urantia is out of step with this normal sequence, the list serves as a standard for understanding our own world's history.

L156.t: Five Personal Transformations and Planetary Adjustments for Social Brotherhood
rows: Social fraternity
International and interracial contacts through travel, commerce, and play; a common language
Intellectual cross-fertilization
Exchange of national and racial literature; ignorance breeds suspicion
Ethical awakening
Unmasks the immorality of human intolerance and the sinfulness of fratricidal strife
Political wisdom
Civilized adjudication substituted for the barbarous arbitrament of war
Spiritual insight
Brotherhood is predicated on the recognition of the fatherhood of God
L156.d: Even on normal evolutionary worlds the world-wide brotherhood of man is not easily achieved, and on a confused and spiritually isolated planet like Urantia it requires much longer time and far greater effort. Jesus has shown the way to immediate spiritual brotherhood, but social brotherhood depends on five transformations and adjustments: social contact through travel and commerce, exchange of literature and thought, ethical awakening that condemns intolerance and fratricidal strife, political wisdom that substitutes adjudication for war, and spiritual insight. The sequence deepens from outward contact to inner conscience and spirit. The last item is the key. Brotherhood is predicated on recognizing the fatherhood of God, and spiritual pressure from above is the only technique for accelerating social evolution.

L157.t: The Three Heads of the Lucifer Declaration of Liberty
rows: The reality of the Universal Father
The Father did not really exist; a myth invented by the Paradise Sons
The universe government of the Creator Son—Michael
Local systems should be autonomous; the Ancients of Days had no right to interfere
The attack upon the universal plan of ascendant mortal training
Too much time and energy spent preparing mortals for an unknown destiny
L157.d: Whatever the early origins of trouble in the hearts of Lucifer and Satan, the final outbreak took form as the Lucifer Declaration of Liberty. The cause of the rebels was stated under three heads. First, the Universal Father did not really exist but was a myth; second, the local systems should be autonomous, rejecting the rule of Michael and the Ancients of Days; third, the plan of ascendant mortal training was a waste spent on a destiny of pure fiction. The structure moves from the denial of God through defiance of universe government to derision of the eternal destiny of mortals. It is a declaration that tears down faith, order, and hope in turn. The narrative records that with such a Declaration of Liberty Lucifer launched his orgy of darkness and death.

L158.t: Twelve Reasons in the Wisdom of Delay
rows: Mercy requires that every wrongdoer have sufficient time to formulate a fully chosen attitude
Justice will never destroy that which mercy can save
No affectionate father is ever precipitate in visiting punishment
Wisdom and love admonish the upright children to bear with an erring brother
The Creator Son had not then completed his bestowal career
The Ancients of Days refused to overrule the Michael decisions
Immanuel counseled allowing rebellion a natural course of self-obliteration
The Faithful of Days advised allowing the rebels free course to the end
Full opportunity for every creature to mature a deliberate choice
The Divine Minister directed that nothing be done to hide rebellion
Summary suppression would lead astray at least three times the number of beings
Time, even in a universe of time, is relative
L158.d: Why were Lucifer and his confederates not sooner interned or adjudicated? An author is permitted to recite twelve of the many reasons known to him. The first four arise from divine character: mercy, justice dominated by a Father's love, patience, and the family wisdom of bearing with an erring brother. The next seven are the judgments and counsel of Michael, the Ancients of Days, Immanuel, the Faithful of Days, the representative of the Supreme Executive, the Divine Minister, and an emergency council of ex-mortals. The last is the relativity of time. The author adds that on Uversa forty-eight reasons are taught for permitting evil to run its full course. Allowing evil full disclosure, rather than hastily suppressing it, protects the free choice of every creature.

L159.t: The Seven Stages of Light and Life
rows: The first or planetary stage
The second or system stage
The third or constellation stage
The fourth or local universe stage
The fifth or minor sector stage
The sixth or major sector stage
The seventh or superuniverse stage
L159.d: The era of light and life is the highest development an evolutionary world attains, yet even this era unfolds in seven stages rather than all at once. The stages are named planetary, system, constellation, local universe, minor sector, major sector, and superuniverse, widening along the units of universe organization. The settling of one world is linked with the settling of the larger units that surround it. At the same time the narrative adds that the planetary values of any stage may be attained by any world quite independent of the development of other worlds. It also notes that the worlds of the Spirit-fused mortals evolve along lines identical with those of the Adjuster-fusion series. Progress has no end; even a settled world keeps growing toward a larger cosmic completion.

L160.t: Four Disbursements of the Tithe on a World Settled in Light and Life
rows: Three per cent
The promotion of truth—science, education, and philosophy
Three per cent
Beauty—play, social leisure, and art
Three per cent
Goodness—social service, altruism, and religion
One per cent
Insurance reserves against accident, disease, old age, or unpreventable disasters
L160.d: Human government in the conduct of material affairs continues to function throughout the age of light and life. A world in the first stage which the author recently visited financed its public activities by the tithing technique. All able-bodied citizens worked at something, and every adult worker paid ten per cent of his income or increase to the public treasury. The funds were disbursed in four ways: three per cent to truth, three per cent to beauty, three per cent to goodness, and one per cent to insurance reserves against incapacity for labor. Notably, the three supreme values of truth, beauty, and goodness share most of the public budget equally. Taxes go not to armaments or power but to science, art, and service. The budget shows in concrete form what a settled society treasures.

L161.t: Seven Groups of Qualified Administrators of a Settled Planet
rows: Young Material Sons and Daughters brought from the system headquarters
The progeny of the semimortal staff of the Planetary Prince
The direct planetary progeny of Adam and Eve
Materialized and humanized midway creatures
Mortals of Adjuster-fusion status temporarily exempted from translation
Specially trained mortals of the planetary schools of administration
Certain elective commissions of three properly qualified citizens
L161.d: A planet the size of Urantia, when fairly well settled, would have about one hundred subadministrative centers, each presided over by one of seven groups of qualified administrators. The list begins with young Material Sons and Daughters from the system headquarters, passes through the progeny of the Prince's staff, the direct progeny of Adam and Eve, and humanized midway creatures, and comes down to mortals: those of Adjuster-fusion status who petition to delay translation, those trained in the schools of administration, and elective commissions of three citizens. Beings from above and beings grown on the planet rule together, and in the end even the vote of ordinary citizens has its place. The administration of a settled world combines guidance from above with participation from below.

L162.t: Administrative Adjustments in the Seven Stages of Light and Life
rows: The first stage
Three rulers: Planetary Sovereign, chief of finaliters, and Adam and Eve
The second stage
A Life Carrier arrives as volunteer adviser to purify and stabilize the race
The third stage
A new appreciation of the Ancients of Days
The fourth stage
Trinity Teacher Sons come as volunteer counselors and advisers
The fifth stage
Readjustments of the physical domains; concern of the Master Physical Controllers
The sixth stage
New functions of the mind circuits of the realm
The seventh stage
Advisers from the Ancients of Days and the Supreme Executive join
L162.d: Even after an evolutionary world is settled in light and life, administration does not stand still but is readjusted at every stage. In the first stage the Planetary Sovereign, the chief of finaliters, and Adam and Eve rule together, with liberated midwayers serving as interpreters. In the second a Life Carrier helps purify the race; in the third new relations are formed with the Ancients of Days. In the fourth the Trinity Teacher Sons come as counselors; the fifth is marked by physical readjustments, the sixth by new functions of the mind circuits, and the seventh by the joining of superuniverse advisers. Attention widens from body to mind and from planet to superuniverse. A settled world is not a finished standstill but a succession of increasingly brilliant attainment.

L163.t: Five Careers Open to a Planetary Adam and Eve upon Release
rows: Secure planetary release and start out immediately on the Paradise career
Receive Adjusters with their volunteering pure-line children, then go to universe headquarters
Go direct to the midsonite world, there to receive their Adjusters
Return to the system headquarters to occupy seats on the supreme court
Serve as teachers on their native world for a season
L163.d: A Planetary Adam and Eve are the Material Son and Daughter who come to uplift the races of an evolutionary world biologically. Their assignment lasts long into the era of light and life, and upon release they may select one of five careers. They may start the Paradise career at once, receive Adjusters together with their children, go to the midsonite world, serve on the system supreme court, or teach for a season on their native world before departing. All five paths finally lead to receiving Adjusters and ascending to Paradise. Notably, even Sons and Daughters who descended to serve eventually enter the ascending path like mortals. Service and ascension form one cycle in the universe.

L164.t: Three Elements in the Attainment of Cosmologic Levels of Thought
rows: Curiosity
Hunger for harmony and thirst for beauty
Aesthetic appreciation
Love of the beautiful and appreciation of the artistic touch of all creative manifestations
Ethic sensitivity
Even cosmology leads to the pursuit of divine reality values—to God-consciousness
L164.d: The worlds settled in light and life are deeply concerned with the comprehension of truth, beauty, and goodness, because these quality values embrace the revelation of Deity to the realms of time and space. In this context the narrative says the attainment of cosmologic levels of thought includes three things: curiosity that hungers for harmony, aesthetic appreciation that loves the artistic touch in creation on all levels, and ethic sensitivity that, through the realization of truth, recognizes divine goodness. The structure moves from curiosity to beauty and from beauty to goodness. The key is that the study of the cosmos does not remain dry knowledge but finally leads to God-consciousness. Science, art, and morality are joined in a single path.

rows: Inspector number 811,307 reported space conditions favorable for materialization
The Uversa Council of Equilibrium issued a permit to dispatch a force organizer
The enormous Andronover nebula number 876,926 was duly initiated
Andronover well established as one of the primary nebulae of Orvonton
The Andronover system was assuming gigantic proportions
The height of the energy-mobilization period; maximum of mass
The first Andronover sun was born
The recaptive period of the Andronover nebula began
Solar circuits well established; the staff of Michael arrived on Salvington
Contraction and condensation of the nuclear mass; the oldest inhabited worlds of Nebadon
The nebular apex of condensation tension was reached
The height of the sun-family stage
The first period of sun dispersion was completed
The completion of the tertiary cycle of nebular life
The quartan cycle of Andronover began
The terrific terminal eruption began
The height of the Andronover terminal breakup
The end of the terminal breakup and the birth of your sun
Your sun was a comparatively isolated blazing orb
The enormous Angona system began its approach
The organization of the Jupiter and Saturn systems
The condensation nucleuses of the other ten planets were well formed
The solar system was functioning much as it does today
Urantia was about one tenth its present mass
The earth began decidedly to gain on the moon
The earth was two thirds its present size
The actual beginning of Urantia history
950,000,000 years ago
One great continent of land and one large body of water, the Pacific Ocean
900,000,000 years ago
The first Satania scouting party arrived on Urantia
850,000,000 years ago
The first real epoch of the stabilization of the earth's crust began
800,000,000 years ago
The first great land epoch, the age of increased continental emergence
750,000,000 years ago
The first breaks in the continental land mass began
700,000,000 years ago
Conditions suitable for the support of life were ripening
650,000,000 years ago
Further extension of the continental seas, reaching the needed saltiness
L165.d: The prelife history of Urantia is recorded not as a numbered list but as a chain of dates, each beginning "⟦Q 57:0.2⟧years ago⟦/Q⟧." The authors reckon time by the calendar of 365¼ days and use the nearest whole numbers, though exact years are of record. The chronology begins 987 billion years ago with an inspector's report and runs through the birth and breakup of the Andronover nebula, the birth of your sun, the approach of the Angona system and the formation of the solar system, and the growth of earth and moon, to the time when continents and seas were ready to receive life. The intervals narrow from hundreds of billions of years to fifty million. Even the physical history of the cosmos is a planned process under the supervision of force organizers and controllers.

L166.t: The Five Major Eras of Urantia History
rows: The prelife era (Archeozoic)
The initial four hundred and fifty million years
The life-dawn era (Proterozoic)
The next one hundred and fifty million years
The marine-life era (Paleozoic)
The next two hundred and fifty million years
The early land-life era (Mesozoic)
The next one hundred million years
The mammalian era (Cenozoic)
The last fifty million years
L166.d: The Life Carriers reckon the history of Urantia as beginning about one billion years ago and extending through five major eras: the prelife era from the planet's attaining its present size to the establishment of life, the life-dawn era, the marine-life era when the seas teemed with life, the early land-life era when life emerged onto land, and the mammalian era. The narrative pairs each era with the Archeozoic, Proterozoic, Paleozoic, Mesozoic, and Cenozoic of present-day students, connecting revelation with the terms of human science. The prelife era is the longest and the mammalian era the shortest, while the marine-life era covers about one quarter of planetary history. The evolution of life accelerated after a vast period of preparation.

L167.t: Four Sorts of Sedimentary Deposits of the Early Marine-Life Era
rows: Conglomerates
Matter deposited near the shore lines
Sandstones
Shallow water where the waves were sufficient to prevent mud settling
Shales
The deeper and more quiet water
Limestone
Including the deposits of trilobite shells in deep water
L167.d: In the first period of the marine-life era, life was confined to the inland seas and the oceanic shore line, and the trilobites flourished. The sedimentary deposits of these ages are of four sorts: conglomerates near the shore lines, sandstones in shallow water where waves prevented mud settling, shales in deeper and quieter water, and limestone including trilobite shells in deep water. The list moves from shore to open sea and from shallow to deep water. Each kind of deposit is thus a record of the depth and motion of ancient seas. The narrative then adds that the animals developing from the three original life implantations differed slightly by region. The rock layers of geology are a book of the chronicle of life, and revelation shows how to read it.

L168.t: Five Immense Survival Advantages of Mammals
rows: Bring forth relatively mature and well-developed offspring
Nourish, nurture, and protect their offspring with affectionate regard
Employ their superior brain power in self-perpetuation
Utilize increased agility in escaping from enemies
Apply superior intelligence to environmental adjustment and adaptation
L168.d: As the mammalian era opened, basic mammalian instincts began to be manifested in primitive mammalian types. The narrative lists five reasons why mammals possess an immense survival advantage over all other forms of animal life: they bring forth relatively mature offspring, nurture and protect them with affectionate regard, employ superior brain power, utilize increased agility, and apply superior intelligence to environmental adaptation. The first two concern care for offspring; the last three concern brain, body, and intelligence. Notably, affectionate regard is counted as a survival advantage. Parental love is not a luxury of evolution but a power for survival. On these advantages was laid the foundation from which the human home and intellect would later grow.

L169.t: The Six Sangik Races of Urantia
rows: The red man
The first of the Sangik children to develop a tribal civilization and government
The orange man
A peculiar urge to build, to build anything and everything
The yellow man
The first to abandon the chase and develop a home life based on agriculture
The green man
One of the less able groups, weakened by extensive migrations
The blue man
A great people with the brain power of the red man and the soul of the yellow
The indigo race
The least progressive; they journeyed to Africa
L169.d: On an average evolutionary planet the six races of color appear one by one, but on Urantia all six emerged simultaneously and in one family, which was most unusual. The narrative describes in turn the traits and migrations of the red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and indigo races. The red man was the most intelligent and first developed tribal government; the yellow man most successfully fostered civilization through settled life and brotherhood; the blue man combined brain power with soul and sentiment and was most favored by the descendants of Adam. The order follows the colors of the spectrum and largely the degree of progress. The narrative then explains that racial variety is needed for natural selection, healthy competition, and the development of tolerance and altruism. Human differences were part of the evolutionary plan.

L170.t: Three Distinct Levels of Life Production and Evolution
rows: The physical-energy domain
Mind-capacity production
The mind ministry of the adjutant spirits
Impinging upon spirit capacity
The spirit endowment of mortal mind
Culminating in Thought Adjuster bestowal
L170.d: Basic evolutionary material life is the formulation of the Master Physical Controllers and the life-impartation ministry of the Seven Master Spirits in conjunction with the active ministration of the Life Carriers. Upon this threefold creativity, life production and evolution proceed on three levels: the physical-energy domain produces capacity for mind, the mind ministry of the adjutant spirits impinges upon spirit capacity, and the spirit endowment of mortal mind culminates in the bestowal of the Thought Adjuster. The structure ascends from matter to mind and from mind to spirit. The narrative stresses that because the integrated functioning of these agencies conditions organic evolution, evolution is always purposeful and never accidental. Evolution and creation do not stand opposed.

L171.t: The Threefold Nature of the Corporeal Staff
rows: Corporeal and relatively human
They embodied the Andonic life plasm of Urantia
Material but superhuman beings
Reconstituted as unique men and women of a high and special order
Personally immortal, or undying
The antidotal complements of the life currents circulated through them
L171.d: The one hundred members of the corporeal staff who came with the Planetary Prince Caligastia were volunteers from the ascending mortals of Jerusem. They began their mission on Urantia as extraordinary threefold beings. First, they were corporeal and relatively human, embodying the Andonic life plasm. Second, they were material but superhuman, possessing souls of ascendant growth and reconstituted as men and women of a high and special order. Third, they were personally immortal, since the life currents of the system circulated through their forms. They were human yet superhuman, clothed in mortal bodies yet undying. This threefold nature made them a fitting bridge to teach primitive mankind. Yet when rebellion cut them off from the life circuits they lost their immortality, showing that heavenly privilege depended on loyalty.

L172.t: The Ten Councils of the One Hundred
rows: The council on food and material welfare
Ang
The board of animal domestication and utilization
Bon
The advisers regarding the conquest of predatory animals
Dan
The faculty on dissemination and conservation of knowledge
Fad
The commission on industry and trade
Nod
The college of revealed religion
Hap
The guardians of health and life
Lut
The planetary council on art and science
Mek
The governors of advanced tribal relations
Tut
The supreme court of tribal co-ordination and racial co-operation
Van
L172.d: The Caligastia one hundred were organized in ten autonomous councils of ten members each, and joint sessions were presided over by Daligastia. The ten councils divided among themselves every field primitive mankind needed: food and water, animal domestication, protection from predators, education and writing, industry and trade, religion, sanitation, art and science, the advancement of society to statehood, and a supreme court serving as the court of appeals for the other nine. Fad formulated the first alphabet of twenty-five characters, the first commercial credit was practiced under Nod's council, and Hap's group sought to substitute Creator fear for creature fear. The structure rises from the needs of survival to knowledge, religion, and government. It shows how early civilization might have flowered but for rebellion.

L173.t: “The Father’s Way”: The Seven Commands of Dalamatia
rows: You shall not fear nor serve any God but the Father of all
You shall not disobey the Father's Son, the world's ruler, nor show disrespect to his superhuman associates
You shall not speak a lie when called before the judges of the people
You shall not kill men, women, or children
You shall not steal your neighbor's goods or cattle
You shall not touch your friend's wife
You shall not show disrespect to your parents or to the elders of the tribe
L173.d: This moral law was presented to the early races by Hap, one of the staff of the Planetary Prince Caligastia. The text records that it was the law of Dalamatia for almost three hundred thousand years, and that it became the custom to hold one of these commands in mind for each day of the week, using it for salutations and mealtime thanksgiving. Hundreds of thousands of years later these seven commands closely resemble the Ten Commandments of Moses: the worship of one God, the prohibitions of false witness, murder, theft, and adultery, and respect for parents. Human morality did not descend all at once; the seeds of ancient revelation blossomed again across the ages.

L174.t: Three General Classes of Human Institutions
rows: The institutions of self-maintenance
Industry, property, war for gain, and all the regulative machinery of society
The institutions of self-perpetuation
Home, school, family life, education, ethics, religion, marriage customs, war for defense
The institutions of self-gratification
Dress and adornment, social usages, war for glory, dancing, amusement, games
L174.d: The institutions of human society grow out of basic instincts. The narrative divides them into three classes: institutions of self-maintenance arising from food hunger and self-preservation, institutions of self-perpetuation arising from sex hunger, maternal instinct, and the higher tender emotions, and institutions of self-gratification arising from vanity and pride. It is interesting that war appears in all three classes: war for gain, war for defense, and war for glory. The narrative also adds that civilization has never evolved distinctive institutions of self-gratification. The three groups are minutely interdependent and function as a single social mechanism. To understand institutions one must first see the instincts and emotions beneath them.

L175.t: Five Divisions of Labor in Primitive Society
rows: Specialization based on sex
Modification consequent upon age and disease
Differentiation based on religion
Master and slave
Differentiation based on diverse physical and mental endowments
L175.d: The divisions of labor in primitive society were determined first by natural, and then by social, circumstances. The narrative gives five steps in the early order of specialization: the division of woman as routine worker caring for the child and man as hunter and fighter; the old men and cripples set to making tools and weapons; the medicine men, the first professional class exempted from physical toil; slavery growing out of conquest; and differentiation by inherent endowments. The rivalry of smiths and medicine men, pictured as the first contest between science and religion, is striking. The narrative frankly says that all human beings are not born equal. The differentiation of labor was both an engine of civilization and a root of inequality.

L176.t: Eight Basic Urges Which Led to the Accumulation of Capital
rows: Hunger
Associated with foresight
Love of family
Desire to provide for their wants
Vanity
Longing to display one's property accumulations
Position
Eagerness to buy social and political prestige
Power
The craving to be master
Fear of the ghosts of the dead
Priest fees for protection
Sex urge
The desire to buy one or more wives
Numerous forms of self-gratification
Wealth for power, property for ease, squandering on luxury
L176.d: Capital represents the saving of property in spite of the pressure of the wants of today in order to insure against the demands of the future. The narrative lists eight basic urges that led primitive man to accumulate capital: hunger with foresight, love of family, vanity, position, power, fear of the ghosts of the dead, the sex urge, and numerous forms of self-gratification. Noble and base motives are mixed together. Beside saving for one's family stands the craving to enslave by moneylending, and the priesthoods, thanks to fear of ghosts, became chief among ancient capitalists. As civilization developed, men acquired new incentives for saving. At the root of economic institutions lie both the light and the shadow of human nature.

L177.t: Four Strong Human Proclivities Against Primitive Communism
rows: The family
The desire to bequeath capital goods to one's progeny
Religious tendencies
Saving property as a nucleus for starting life in the next existence
The desire for liberty and leisure
Refusing to make the worker slave to the idler
The urge for security and power
Successful individuals escaping enslavement to shiftless idlers
L177.d: Primitive communism was indispensable scaffolding in the growth of primitive society. But it put a premium on inactivity and idleness, stifled industry, and destroyed ambition, so it gave way to a higher social order. The narrative finds the reason in four strong human proclivities: the family's desire to bequeath property to its progeny, the religious tendency to save up property for the next existence, the desire for liberty and leisure that refuses to make the worker slave to the idler, and the urge for security and power. The key point is that institutions running counter to human nature cannot long endure. The narrative adds that with the passing of communism the home had its beginning and polygamy was gradually displaced by monogamy. Social evolution advances with the current of human nature.

rows: Hunger
Which led to food raids
Woman scarcity
An attempt to relieve a shortage of domestic help
Vanity
The desire to exhibit tribal prowess
Slaves
Need of recruits for the labor ranks
Revenge
When a neighboring tribe was believed to have caused a tribesman's death
Recreation
War was looked upon as recreation by the young men
Religion
The desire to make converts to the cult
L178.d: Warfare persists because man is human, evolved from an animal, and all animals are bellicose. The narrative names seven early causes of war: hunger, woman scarcity, vanity, the need for slaves, revenge, recreation, and religion. The list begins with the needs of survival, passes through emotion and sport, and ends with faith. The last cause weighs heavily. The primitive religions all sanctioned war, and the early priesthoods were usually allied with the military power. Only in recent times has religion begun to frown upon war, and the narrative calls the attempt to separate church and state one of the great peace moves of the ages. To achieve peace we must first understand the roots of the instincts and institutions that produce war.

L179.t: Five Social Values of War to Past Civilizations
rows: Imposed discipline, enforced co-operation
Put a premium on fortitude and courage
Fostered and solidified nationalism
Destroyed weak and unfit peoples
Dissolved the illusion of primitive equality and selectively stratified society
L179.d: War is evil, yet the narrative frankly acknowledges that it had a certain social value to past civilizations. It imposed discipline and co-operation, put a premium on courage, solidified nationalism, destroyed weak peoples, and dissolved the illusion of primitive equality by stratifying society. A qualification follows at once: like slavery, war must sometime be abandoned as civilization advances. The travel and cultural intercourse once promoted by war are now better served by modern transport and communication, and modern struggles disrupt civilized culture. As physicians once believed in bloodletting and later found better remedies, so the international bloodletting of war must give place to better methods. Past usefulness cannot justify present practice.

L180.t: Six Perils of Budding Industry on Urantia
rows: The strong drift toward materialism
Spiritual blindness
The worship of wealth-power
Value distortion
The vices of luxury
Cultural immaturity
The increasing dangers of indolence
Service insensitivity
The growth of undesirable racial softness
Biologic deterioration
The threat of standardized industrial slavery
Personality stagnation
L180.d: The nations of Urantia have entered upon the gigantic struggle between nationalistic militarism and industrialism, a conflict the narrative compares to the agelong struggle between the herder-hunter and the farmer. Industrialism is the more civilized course, but to triumph it must avoid six perils: materialism and spiritual blindness, the worship of wealth-power, the vices of luxury, indolence and service insensitivity, racial softness, and standardized industrial slavery that stagnates personality. Each item pairs an outward tendency with its inner consequence. The saying that labor is ennobling but drudgery is benumbing sums up the list. The success of industrial civilization depends not on material prosperity but on preserving spiritual values and individual originality.

L181.t: Six Common Interests of the Blood-Tie Clans
rows: Tracing origin back to a common ancestor
Allegiance to a common religious totem
Speaking the same dialect
Sharing a common dwelling place
Fearing the same enemies
Having had a common military experience
L181.d: The clans were blood-tie groups within the tribe, and they owed their existence to certain common interests. The narrative lists six: a common ancestor, a common religious totem, the same dialect, a common dwelling place, fear of the same enemies, and a common military experience. The list begins with lineage, passes through faith, language, and land, and ends with shared fear and war. What binds people is not blood alone but the memory of believing, speaking, living, and fighting together. The clan headmen were always subordinate to the tribal chief, and early tribal governments were loose confederations of clans. Larger communities such as the state grew out of these small bonds. The list is a starting point for understanding the principles of social integration.

L182.t: Four Reasons for the Secrecy of the Secret Societies
rows: Fear of incurring the displeasure of the rulers because of the violation of some taboo
In order to practice minority religious rites
For the purpose of preserving valuable "spirit" or trade secrets
For the enjoyment of some special charm or magic
L182.d: Religious cults and political clubs first appeared as secret societies. The narrative gives four reasons for their secrecy: fear of displeasing the rulers by violating some taboo, the practice of minority religious rites, the preservation of valuable spirit or trade secrets, and the enjoyment of some special charm or magic. Different motives of fear, faith, profit, and mystery are gathered together. The narrative then explains that secrecy itself conferred on members the power of mystery over the rest of the tribe and also appealed to vanity; the initiates were the social aristocracy of their day. Originally wholly religious, these societies subsequently became regulative. The list reveals an old principle of human society: what is hidden becomes power.

L183.t: Ten Reasons Society Became Grouped in Classes
rows: Natural
Contact, kinship, and marriage
Personal
The recognition of ability, endurance, skill, and fortitude
Chance
War and emigration resulted in the separating of human groups
Economic
Rich and poor
Geographic
Urban or rural settlement
Social
Popular estimate of the social worth of different groups
Vocational
Castes and guilds
Religious
The early cult clubs produced their own classes
Racial
Color castes
Age
Youth and maturity
L183.d: As society emerged from savagery to barbarism, its members tended to become grouped in classes. The narrative gives ten general reasons: kinship and marriage, personal ability, the chance of war and emigration, wealth and poverty, city and country, popular estimate of social worth, vocation, religion, race, and age. Inborn conditions, acquired abilities, chance, and institutions are all mixed together. The narrative warns that flexible and shifting classes are indispensable to an evolving civilization, but when class becomes caste, social stability is purchased by diminishment of personal initiative. The problem is not class itself but its petrifaction. In judging a social structure one must ask whether the way of movement remains open.

L184.t: Three Intelligent Manipulations for Obliterating Social Classes
rows: Biologic renovation of the racial stocks
Educational training of the increased brain power
Religious quickening of the feelings of mortal kinship and brotherhood
L184.d: Classes in society, having naturally formed, do not easily disappear. The narrative says they will persist until man gradually achieves their evolutionary obliteration through intelligent manipulation of the biologic, intellectual, and spiritual resources of a progressing civilization. There are three means: biologic renovation of the racial stocks through the selective elimination of inferior strains, educational training of the increased brain power that results, and the religious quickening of the feelings of mortal kinship and brotherhood. The structure ascends from body to mind and from mind to spirit. Classes are not abolished at once by decree or revolution; biology, education, and religion together reduce the roots of inequality over long ages. The last means, the feeling of brotherhood, completes the other two.

L185.t: Ten Rights Society Asserts at the Present Time
rows: Assurance of food supply
Military defense—security through preparedness
Internal peace preservation—prevention of personal violence and social disorder
Sex control—marriage, the family institution
Property—the right to own
Fostering of individual and group competition
Provision for educating and training youth
Promotion of trade and commerce—industrial development
Improvement of labor conditions and rewards
The guarantee of the freedom of religious practices
L185.d: Nature confers no rights on man, only life and a world in which to live it. The list of rights was built up as society gradually asserted them. The narrative gives ten at the present time: food supply, military defense, internal peace, marriage and the family, property, competition, education of youth, trade and industry, labor conditions, and religious freedom. The list begins with the basics of survival and ends with religious freedom, whose purpose is that all other social activities may be exalted by becoming spiritually motivated. The narrative says that rights old beyond knowledge of origin are often called natural rights, but human rights are entirely social, no more than the ever-changing rules of the game. Preserving rights is finally a matter of social wisdom and responsibility.

L186.t: Four Ways Property Disputes Were Handled
rows: By destroying the disputed property
By force—the contestants fought it out
By arbitration—a third party decided
By appeal to the elders—later to the courts
L186.d: When property appeared, disputes over property appeared with it. The narrative lists four ways primitive society handled them: destroying the disputed property, letting the contestants fight it out, arbitration by a third party, and appeal to the elders and later to the courts. The sequence reflects the history of legal development, moving from destruction and violence through arbitration to institutional adjudication. The narrative adds that the first courts were regulated fistic encounters and the judges merely umpires. "⟦Q 70:11.13⟧Might was still right⟦/Q⟧," but later verbal arguments were substituted for physical blows. Institutions of justice grew through the long process of confining force within rules, and civilization is the history of replacing violence with reason.

L187.t: Twelve Dangers to Be Prevented for Men to Maintain Their Freedom
rows: Usurpation of unwarranted power by either the executive or legislative branches
Machinations of ignorant and superstitious agitators
Retardation of scientific progress
Stalemate of the dominance of mediocrity
Domination by vicious minorities
Control by ambitious and clever would-be dictators
Disastrous disruption of panics
Exploitation by the unscrupulous
Taxation enslavement of the citizenry by the state
Failure of social and economic fairness
Union of church and state
Loss of personal liberty
L187.d: If men would maintain their freedom, they must, after choosing their charter of liberty, provide for its wise, intelligent, and fearless interpretation. The narrative names twelve things to be prevented: usurpation of power, agitators, retardation of science, the dominance of mediocrity, vicious minorities, would-be dictators, panics, exploitation, taxation enslavement, failure of fairness, the union of church and state, and loss of personal liberty. The threats come from many directions: abuse of power, social stagnation, economic injustice, and the politicizing of religion. The last item sums up what all the others protect. These, the narrative says, are the purposes of constitutional tribunals acting as governors upon the engines of representative government. Freedom is harder to keep than to win.

L188.t: Eight Lacks That Kept the Red Man from Statehood
rows: Acquirement and inheritance of private property
Cities plus agriculture and industry
Helpful domestic animals
Practical family organization
Definite territory
A strong executive head
Enslavement of captives
Decisive conquests
L188.d: The northern tribes of the American red men never progressed beyond a loose confederation of tribes to real statehood. Their nearest approach was the Iroquois federation, but this group of six nations failed to survive because it lacked eight essentials of modern national life: inheritance of private property, cities with agriculture and industry, domestic animals, practical family organization, definite territory, a strong executive head, enslavement of captives, and decisive conquests. The red men clung to the mother-family and nephew inheritance and either adopted or massacred their captives. The narrative judges that they were too democratic; they had a good government, but it failed. Had they not prematurely encountered the white man's civilization, they would eventually have evolved a state. States grow not from ideals alone but on economic and social foundations.

L189.t: The Foundations of the Successful Roman State
rows: The father-family
Agriculture and the domestication of animals
Condensation of population—cities
Private property and land
Slavery—classes of citizenship
Conquest and reorganization of weak and backward peoples
Definite territory with roads
Personal and strong rulers
L189.d: In tracing the evolution of the state, Paper 71 takes Rome as its outstanding example. The Roman state rested on the father-family, agriculture and domesticated animals, cities, and private property in land, and was carried further by slavery and classes of citizenship, the conquest and reorganization of weaker peoples, a definite territory with roads, and strong personal rulers. The sequence moves from family and economy outward to territory and power, the typical path of state formation. Yet the text immediately names Rome's weakness as well: reforms adopted too suddenly and extensively, and too rapid extension associated with internal degeneration. The list invites the reader to weigh the foundations of success alongside the causes of collapse.

rows: Glorification of mediocrity
Choice of base and ignorant rulers
Failure to recognize the basic facts of social evolution
Danger of universal suffrage in the hands of uneducated and indolent majorities
Slavery to public opinion; the majority is not always right
L190.d: Democracy is an ideal, but it is a product of civilization, not of evolution. So the text counsels, go slowly and select carefully, and then names five dangers: the glorification of mediocrity, the choice of base and ignorant rulers, blindness to the basic facts of social evolution, universal suffrage in the hands of uneducated and indolent majorities, and slavery to public opinion. All five arise when the wisdom and education of the electorate fall short. The text adds that the education of public opinion is the only safe and true method of accelerating civilization. This is not a warning to abandon democracy but a reminder that a democracy can mature only as its citizens mature.

rows: Freedom of the person
Slavery, serfdom, and all forms of human bondage must disappear
Freedom of the mind
A free people educated—taught to think intelligently and plan wisely
The reign of law
The will and whims of rulers replaced by legislative enactments
Freedom of speech
Freedom of all forms of expression for human aspirations and opinions
Security of property
The right to use, control, bestow, sell, lease, and bequeath property
The right of petition
The right of citizens to be heard
The right to rule
The power of petition progresses to the actual management of government
Universal suffrage
An intelligent, efficient, and universal electorate
Control of public servants
Wise techniques of guiding and controlling officeholders
Intelligent and trained representation
Electing only the technically trained, competent, loyal, and morally fit
L191.d: Practical and efficient representative government is not founded overnight; it evolves through ten steps. The first is freedom of the person, release from all bondage, followed by freedom of the mind through education. Upon these rest the reign of law, freedom of speech, and security of property, while the citizen's voice grows from the right of petition to the right to rule. The last three steps, universal suffrage, control of public servants, and intelligent and trained representation, concern the quality of voters and of those they elect. Freedom comes first, yet freedom without education usually does more harm than good, and in the end the survival of democracy depends on electing only those fit for public office.

L192.t: Three Mighty Drives of the Ideal State
rows: Love loyalty derived from the realization of human brotherhood
Intelligent patriotism based on wise ideals
Cosmic insight interpreted in terms of planetary facts, needs, and goals
L192.d: The ideal state is moved not by coercion or fear but by three mighty and co-ordinated drives. The first is love loyalty arising from the realization of human brotherhood; the second is intelligent patriotism, based on wise ideals rather than blind allegiance; the third is cosmic insight interpreted in terms of the facts, needs, and goals of the planet. When love, intelligence, and spiritual insight work together, a state attains a high level. The text goes on to say that the laws of the ideal state are few in number, having passed out of the negativistic taboo age into an era of individual liberty grounded in enhanced self-control. The more mature the inner life of the citizens, the fewer the outward laws required.

L193.t: Twelve Programs of an Expanding Civilization
rows: Preservation of individual liberties
Protection of the home
Promotion of economic security
Prevention of disease
Compulsory education
Compulsory employment
Profitable utilization of leisure
Care of the unfortunate
Race improvement
Promotion of science and art
Promotion of philosophy—wisdom
Augmentation of cosmic insight—spirituality
L193.d: These are the twelve features of the progressive program of an expanding civilization. They begin with individual liberty and the protection of the home, continue through economic security, disease prevention, compulsory education and employment, the profitable use of leisure, and care of the unfortunate, and then rise through race improvement and the promotion of science and art to philosophy and wisdom, and finally to the augmentation of cosmic insight and spirituality. The arrangement climbs clearly from material security to intellectual growth to spiritual insight. The text says that such progress leads directly to the social achievement of the brotherhood of man and the personal status of God-consciousness. The goal of civilization, in the end, is the supreme desire to do the will of the Father in heaven.

L194.t: Seven Ascending Levels of Mortal Wisdom
rows: The knowledge of things
The realization of meanings
The appreciation of values
The nobility of work—duty
The motivation of goals—morality
The love of service—character
Cosmic insight—spiritual discernment
L194.d: Education is not something completed in school; it is the business of living and must continue throughout a lifetime, so that mankind may gradually experience the seven ascending levels of mortal wisdom. The knowledge of things comes first, followed by the realization of meanings and the appreciation of values. Then the nobility of work becomes duty, the motivation of goals becomes morality, and the love of service becomes character, until at last one reaches cosmic insight, spiritual discernment. The ascent from facts to meanings and values, and on to character and spiritual discernment, reveals the true purpose of education. The text concludes that by these achievements many will ascend to the mortal ultimate of mind attainment, God-consciousness.

L195.t: Twelve Levels in the Evolution of Statehood
rows: A threefold government of executive, legislative, and judicial branches
The freedom of social, political, and religious activities
The abolition of all forms of slavery and human bondage
The ability of the citizenry to control the levying of taxes
Universal education—learning extended from the cradle to the grave
The proper adjustment between local and national governments
The fostering of science and the conquest of disease
The due recognition of sex equality and co-ordinated functioning of men and women
The elimination of toiling slavery by machine invention
The conquest of dialects—the triumph of a universal language
The ending of war—international adjudication by continental courts
The world-wide pursuit of wisdom and the evolution of a world religion
L195.d: These are the twelve levels through which statehood progresses. The starting point is threefold government of executive, legislative, and judicial branches; the text calls this division the only sacred feature of any human government, for the universe itself is administered by such a segregation of functions. Then follow freedom of activity, abolition of bondage, citizen control of taxation, lifelong education, adjustment of local and national government, science and the conquest of disease, sex equality, liberation from toil by machines, and a universal language. The final two are the ending of war through continental courts, and the exaltation of philosophy with the evolution of a world religion. These are the prerequisites of progressive government; Urantia is far from them, but mankind is on the march.

L196.t: Eight Lists from Government on a Neighboring Planet
rows: Three legislative houses
Upper house, lower house, the third house—the elder statesmen
Three levels of law courts
Minor courts, state supreme courts, federal supreme court
Three divisions of socioeconomic courts
Parental courts, educational courts, industrial courts
Three divisions of legal compensation
Interest on invested capital, salary for skill, wages for labor
Four sources of old-age pension funds
One day's earnings, bequests, compulsory labor in state mines, natural resources
Five sources of federal income
Import duties, royalties, inheritance tax, military equipment, natural resources
Five special schools
Statesmanship, philosophy, science, professional training, military and naval
Five features of the modified voting system
One vote each, merit votes, disenfranchisement, tax brackets, functional voting
L196.d: Paper 72 describes the social and political life of the most advanced continental nation on a neighboring planet in Satania. Like Urantia, this world suffered the disloyalty of its Planetary Prince and the default of its Material Son, yet it achieved a considerable statehood by its own efforts. The paper contains eight numbered lists that present the nation's institutions at a glance: a legislature of three houses, two court systems, the principles of compensation in the industrial courts, the sources of old-age pensions and federal income, the special schools, and the modified voting system. Notable are the restriction of public office to graduates of the schools of statesmanship and the exercise of suffrage by economic and social groups rather than by territory. These lists offer Urantia a concrete example to consider.

L197.t: Seven Subjects Taught in the Garden Schools
rows: Health and the care of the body
The golden rule, the standard of social intercourse
The relation of individual rights to group rights and community obligations
History and culture of the various earth races
Methods of advancing and improving world trade
Co-ordination of conflicting duties and emotions
The cultivation of play, humor, and competitive substitutes for physical fighting
L197.d: The entire purpose of the western school system of the Garden of Eden was socialization. The forenoon recesses were devoted to horticulture and agriculture, the afternoons to competitive play, and the evenings to social intercourse and personal friendships. The instruction covered health and care of the body, the golden rule as the standard of social intercourse, the relation of individual rights to group rights and community obligations, the history and culture of the earth races, the improvement of world trade, the co-ordination of conflicting duties and emotions, and play, humor, and competitive substitutes for fighting. Religious and sexual training, by contrast, were regarded as the province of the home, the duty of parents. This curriculum of body, relationships, and world still shows a balance worth comparing with education today.

L198.t: Seven Heads of the Laws of the Garden
rows: The laws of health and sanitation
The social regulations of the Garden
The code of trade and commerce
The laws of fair play and competition
The laws of home life
The civil codes of the golden rule
The seven commands of supreme moral rule
L198.d: The laws of the Garden of Eden were based on the older codes of Dalamatia and were promulgated under seven heads: health and sanitation, social regulations, trade and commerce, fair play and competition, home life, the civil codes of the golden rule, and the seven commands of supreme moral rule. Beginning with bodily health and moving through society, economy, home, and civic life to the moral commands, the arrangement shows the breadth of the Garden civilization. The text notes that the moral law of Eden differed little from the seven commandments of Dalamatia, but the Adamites taught many additional reasons for them; against murder, for example, they cited the indwelling of the Thought Adjuster. Law was taught not merely as prohibition but as understandable principle.

L199.t: Three Views on the Purpose of the Tower
rows: The largest group, almost one half
A memorial of Nodite history and racial superiority
The next largest faction
To commemorate the Dilmun culture; a center of commerce, art, and manufacture
The smallest and minority contingent
Atonement for the rebellion; devoted to the worship of the Father of all
L199.d: The Nodites began building the tower according to Bablot's plans, but after four and one-half years a great dispute arose over its purpose, and all work stopped. The largest group wanted a memorial of Nodite history and racial superiority; the next faction wished to commemorate the Dilmun culture and foresaw a center of commerce and art. Only the smallest contingent proposed to atone for their progenitors' folly in the Caligastia rebellion by devoting the tower to the worship of the Father of all. The religious group was promptly voted down, and when the other two views could not be settled by debate, the parties fell to fighting. This civil war dispersed the Nodites and set their culture in long decline. The list shows racial pride crowding out a spiritual purpose.

rows: The western or Syrian Nodites
Remnants of the racial memorialists; contributed to the later Assyrian stock
The eastern or Elamite Nodites
The culture and commerce advocates; united with mixed Sangik tribes in Elam
The central or pre-Sumerian Nodites
A small group at the river mouths; blended with Adamites to found the Sumerians
The northern Nodites and Amadonites—the Vanites
Arose before the Bablot conflict; followers of Van and Amadon
L200.d: The civil war over the tower of Babel dispersed the Nodites and produced four great centers, three of them established immediately after the conflict. Those who had wanted a racial memorial journeyed north to become the Syrian Nodites; the culture and commerce advocates migrated east into Elam and mingled with the Sangik tribes. A small group at the mouth of the rivers kept more of its racial integrity and later blended with the Adamites to found the Sumerian peoples of historic times. The fourth, the northern Vanites, arose earlier, descended from those who had forsaken Nod for the leadership of Van and Amadon. The list explains how the Sumerians appeared so suddenly in Mesopotamia with a full-grown and superior culture.

L201.t: Four Groups of the United Midwayers
rows: Midway messengers
A small corps bearing names; quick and reliable personal communication
Planetary sentinels
Guardians of the worlds; patrol the invisible spirit realm of the planet
Contact personalities
Contacts with mortal beings; liaisons of the spiritual and material levels
Progress helpers
The more spiritual midwayers; assistants to the various orders of seraphim
L201.d: Midwayers are neither men nor angels; on Urantia they are organized as the United Midwayers and serve with the planetary seraphim. According to innate endowments and acquired skills they form four groups. The midway messengers, who bear names, provide quick and reliable personal communication; the planetary sentinels patrol the invisible spirit realm of the planet. The contact personalities are employed in all contacts with mortals of the material worlds, including, the text reveals, the subject through whom these communications were transmitted. The progress helpers, the more spiritual of the midway creatures, serve as assistants to the seraphim.
